label: Lists
title: The most popular AI series of 2026, ranked by views
excerpt: From a dragon birth that broke out on TikTok to a monthly fantasy-action saga with 40+ characters, these are the AI series pulling the biggest audiences this year.
body: AI series stopped being a novelty somewhere in 2026, and the view counts finally back that up. Below is this year's ranking by views — alongside two single-installment entries in ongoing AI story-universes that are already pulling series-sized audiences on their own, flagged as such rather than counted as true multi-episode shows.

1. The Mother's Monster — roughly 86 million views. Technically a standalone short, not a serialized show, but its premise carried it past every true series on this list: a mother gives birth to a dragon her village brands a monster, and must protect him from the superstition that surrounds them both. The version published through the MYTHRA channel is the one driving those numbers.

2. The Chronicles of Bone — roughly 34.5 million views. Kavan Cardoza's ongoing monthly fantasy-action series, built around a cast of 40+ characters across five planned seasons, made with Freepik and Magnific.
3. Kade Voss | Bounty Hunter — roughly 9.3 million views. A 7-episode AI-generated sci-fi action series.
4. The Sky-Fallen Legacy — roughly 9 million views. A 13-episode sci-fi series from The Reality Foundry, made with Dreamina and Pippit AI, released July through October 2026.
5. Annunaki: The Nibiru Legacy — roughly 7.5 million views. A 2-episode AI-generated sci-fi series.
6. The Sage: Homecoming — roughly 7 million views. A 7-episode horror series from Phantom X, directed by Mike J Mitch and made with Invideo AI, released March through September 2026.

7. ARK-7 — roughly 4.2 million views. The pilot episode of Serge Karloff's AI sci-fi series, built on a hybrid model of real identity and AI-native production — including Sofia, a young girl whose likeness (used with her mother's permission) makes her the youngest inhabitant of the ARK-7 universe.
Worth noting: these figures are view-count snapshots, not an AIMB-verified leaderboard — we'll revisit the list as 2026 closes out and new episodes land.
